Subject: Request: certification checklist + network diagram for on-prem (Acme HealthTech)

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the product overview last week. As we evaluate a private (on-prem / VPC / air‑gapped) deployment for a pilot, our security and procurement teams need two things to proceed:

1) A one‑page certification checklist describing live requirements for on‑prem / air‑gapped installs (network ports, allowed egress, KMS/HSM requirements, patching cadence, SBOM expectations, etc.).
2) A network diagram template we can drop into our architecture review (showing inbound/outbound connections, optional proxy/egress patterns, storage/KV placement).

Can you also confirm:
- Whether Redwood provides an offline installer package and what the footprint looks like (approx. disk, container images).
- If you support FIPS‑compatible TLS and integration with customer KMS (HSM) for model key material.
- Expected timeline for a security review and a small POC (we’d like targeted sign‑off in 3–4 weeks if possible).

Attachments: I will upload our security questionnaire (standard RFI) separately — for now a checklist and diagram template would let us scope the work.

If useful, loop in your technical owner for on‑prem installs; I’d like a short synchronous call after we get the checklist.

Best,
Lisa Grant
Director, Security & Compliance
Acme HealthTech

Hi Lisa / Alex — adding a few technical clarifications here and a diagram template attached.

Short answers up front:
- Offline installer: yes—we provide a tarball with container images and a package manifest. Typical unpack + local registry push flow. Footprint for a minimal pilot (1 inference node + control plane) is ~35GB compressed images, ~120GB runtime disk (model cache + logs).
- KMS/HSM: we support customer‑managed keys via KMIP for on‑prem HSMs and integrations with AWS/Azure KMS for VPC deployments. We can enable FIPS‑compliant cipher suites if the target HSM and OS are FIPS enabled.
- Egress options: (a) fully air‑gapped with manual patching via customer mirror, (b) restricted egress to update mirror + telemetry disabled, or (c) full egress for updates and metrics. Default for pilot is (b) where we only reach out to customer‑managed mirrors.

Notes for the network diagram template (attached):
- Recommended ports: control plane <-> inference nodes (TLS; customer can NAT), local registry access ports, optional metrics/ELK push to customer collectors.
- Storage: separate model cache volume with encryption at rest; we recommend using LUKS or the platform’s native encryption.
- Audit logs: we can push logs to a customer syslog endpoint or ship a secure archive; retention configurable.

Attachment: network-diagram-template.pdf (application/pdf)

I’ll join the call to review the checklist in detail and to capture any environment constraints.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead, On‑Prem Deployments | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

If easier, we can take a short SOW template from you and return it redlined. Preferred next step: 30‑minute call on Thu to review SOW + pricing.
